subject: Order Form + MSA: venue & interim relief — LumenPay redline
body:
From: Rebecca Torres <r.torres@lumenpay.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form + MSA: governing law & provisional relief

Hi Priyom / Aditya,

Attached is LumenPay's latest MSA redline (v3) and the updated Order Form SOW. Primary items for your legal/ops review: governing law, venue for emergency relief, and whether we carve injunctive relief out of arbitration. To summarize our position:

- Governing law: Commonwealth of Massachusetts.
- Venue for urgent equitable relief: courts located in Suffolk County (Boston), MA. Parties may seek temporary injunctive or provisional remedies there.
- Dispute resolution: binding arbitration for most contractual disputes (JAMS, seat Boston) with an express carveout allowing either party to seek emergency injunctive relief in Suffolk County Superior Court.

We understand Redwood typically prefers arbitration or Delaware law in enterprise MSAs. LumenPay is sensitive to speed for urgent relief and wants a local forum in MA for expedited orders. Please confirm what you can accept and whether we should propose language that narrows the carveout (e.g., only injunctive relief to preserve trade secrets/IP).

Attachments: LumenPay_MSA_redline_v3.docx (redline), OrderForm_SOW_v2.pdf

Thanks,
Rebecca Torres
Senior Counsel, LumenPay
rebecca.torres@lumenpay.com

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Order Form + MSA: governing law & provisional relief

Rebecca — thanks for sending. Quick note from the account side: LumenPay's timeline for go-live is mid-May; procurement needs a short list of negotiable items. Two asks from our side so legal can advise:

1) Can we get a short rationale for asking for MA specifically (is it investor preference / HQ / regulator)?
2) Are you flexible on limiting the injunctive-relief carveout to only IP/data confidentiality/KV cache protection, rather than all equitable relief?

Looping in Kim (legal) for recommended language and whether Redwood can accept a localized court seat. Aditya — may need you for any exec escalation on terms.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

On Wed, Mar 11, 2026 at 09:12 AM kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Rebecca Torres <r.torres@lumenpay.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order Form + MSA: governing law & provisional relief

Team — reviewed LumenPay's redline. High-level position and recommended compromise below (we should present this as a short email to Rebecca to keep momentum):

- Governing law: Redwood prefers Delaware (corporate certainty) but is willing to accept the substantive law of Massachusetts limited to the interpretation of performance obligations under the Order Form only. Proposed clause: "This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, except that disputes arising solely from the Order Form's SOW shall be governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts." This is narrow and preserves our precedent while addressing their operational concerns.

- Injunctive relief carveout: Redwood will accept an express carveout allowing either party to seek interim injunctive or provisional relief in courts of Suffolk County, MA, provided the carveout is narrowly drafted: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek temporary injunctive or other provisional relief in the state or federal courts located in Suffolk County, Commonwealth of Massachusetts, solely to preserve the status quo, prevent irreparable harm, or protect trade secrets and confidential information pending the outcome of arbitration." Key points: (i) limit to provisional measures pending arbitration; (ii) explicitly include injunctive relief to protect trade secrets/IP; (iii) require immediate notice to arbitral tribunal where feasible.

- Arbitration: retain binding arbitration for merits in a neutral forum (JAMS or AAA) with seat as agreed (we can keep Boston as seat to reduce pushback) and an expedited timeline for discovery. For international/regulatory issues we can add a fallback for court jurisdiction where arbitration is not available.

Action: Priyom / Aditya, if you agree, I'll draft the short compromise paragraph and send to Rebecca. If LumenPay insists on full Massachusetts governing law for the entire MSA, that's an escalation to product/legal leadership; let's avoid if possible.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

----
From: Rebecca Torres <r.torres@lumenpay.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form + MSA: governing law & provisional relief

Thanks, Kim and team — that compromise looks reasonable and addresses our business needs. Two quick confirmations from LumenPay:

1) LumenPay will accept Delaware governing law for the MSA with the narrow Order Form carve (governing law of MA for SOW matters) as proposed.
2) LumenPay asks that the injunctive relief carveout language explicitly reference "trade secrets, source code, and confidential customer data" to make enforcement clear.

We will update our redline to reflect acceptance of the split-governing-law approach and mark the injunctive carveout language as agreed with the additional specificity. Please send the final cleanup so procurement can sign and we can move the DocuSign step.

Best,
Rebecca

---
Thread notes: internal ask: prepare a short "clean clause" (single paragraph) implementing Kim's proposed compromise; include redline attachment showing the split-law language and the narrowed injunctive carveout. Procurement timeline: finalize by 2026-03-19 to meet mid-May go-live.
